controls.label: Initial amount N0
controls.help: Sets the starting population: the Remaining amount result scales in direct proportion and both bars in the comparison chart resize, while the Half-life, Decay exponent, Half-lives elapsed and Remaining fraction readouts stay unchanged.

controls.label: Decay constant lambda
controls.help: Sets how fast the population falls: larger values shorten the Half-life intermediate, raise the Decay exponent and the Half-lives elapsed intermediates, and lower the Remaining fraction and Remaining amount at a fixed time.

controls.label: Elapsed time t
controls.help: Slides the observation point along the decay curve: growing time raises the Decay exponent and Half-lives elapsed intermediates and lowers the Remaining fraction and Remaining amount outputs.

explorations.title: Elapsed time equal to one half-life
explorations.instruction: Predict: when the elapsed time equals the half-life, what values do the Remaining fraction and Remaining amount readouts take? Then apply the preset, which sets the decay constant and the elapsed time.
explorations.observe: The Half-life readout shows about 1.00 years, Half-lives elapsed shows about 1.00, Remaining fraction falls to about 0.50 and Remaining amount falls to about 50 from the initial 100.
explorations.why: The preset puts lambda t near ln(2), so the Remaining fraction exp(-lambda t) lands near 0.5, and the Half-lives elapsed ratio t / t_half lands near 1 because the Half-life intermediate ln(2)/lambda was chosen to match the elapsed time.

explorations.title: Doubling the decay constant at fixed time
explorations.instruction: Predict: keeping the elapsed time at 1 year, what happens to the Half-life and Half-lives elapsed readouts when the decay constant doubles? Then apply the preset, which sets the decay constant and the elapsed time.
explorations.observe: The Half-life readout drops to about 0.50 years, Half-lives elapsed rises to about 2.00, Remaining fraction falls to about 0.25 and Remaining amount to about 25.
explorations.why: Half-life is ln(2)/lambda, so doubling lambda halves the Half-life intermediate; at the same elapsed time the Half-lives elapsed ratio doubles and the Remaining fraction becomes exp(-2 ln 2), which is 0.25.
